thread.title: China, Chip, Tech Stocks Lead Futures Rally Ahead Of Payrolls Report

author: Investor's Business Daily
title: China, Chip, Tech Stocks Lead Futures Rally Ahead Of Payrolls Report
text:
3 China, Chip, Tech Names Lead Early Rally As This Burger Chain Breaks Out January 05, 2018, 08:03:04 AM EDT By ALAN R. ELLIOTT,   
The Nasdaq Composite ran at the head of an early rally Friday, as stocks powered past a weaker-than-expected December payrolls report and looked to wrap up a strong first week for 2018. 
[ibd-display-video id=3065146 width=50 float=left autostart=true]The Dow Jones industrial average jumped nearly 0.3% at the open. The S&P 500 oepened 0.2% higher and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.3%, with NetEase ( NTES ), Xilinx ( XLNX ) and Cisco System s ( CSCO ) posting wide early gains. 
The closely-watched December payrolls report showed U.S. nonfarm employers added 148,000 new workers in December, according to the Labor Department. That was a 41% decrease vs. November's hiring and far below consensus projections for a decrease to 191,000 new jobs. Private employers accounted for nearly all of the new hires. Manufacturers were 17% of the total, up slightly vs. November's performance. 
The unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%, and growth in average hourly earnings was also unchanged, up 2.5%. 
The trade deficit widened for a third straight month in November, to $50.5 billion, the Commerce Department reported. That was up from October's $48.9 billion. 
The Commerce Department releases November factory orders estimates at 10 a.m. ET. The Institute for Supply Management delivers its services index for December at 10 a.m. ET. Cisco, Xilinx Surge On Upgrades; Sonic Breaks Out On Q1 Report 
Cisco Systems hammered out the Dow's top opening gain, up 1.3% as the stock aims for new high ground after clearing a cup-with-handle buy point at 34.20 in October. Bank Of America/Merrill Lynch upgraded Cisco to buy, from neutral, and hoisted its price target 24% to 47. 
Apple ( AAPL ) opened 0.4% higher, and heads into Friday's session up more than 2% for the week. Shares are being squeezed in the narrowing margin between a rising 10-week moving average and a 176.34 buy point. 
The FANG stock tech leaders all traded roughly around 0.5% higher, giving the Nasdaq a firm boost. Facebook ( FB ) opened back above its 184.35 buy point. Amazon.com (AMZN) remained just under a buy point at 1213.10. Netflix (NFLX) is still in its buy range after clearing a 204.48 buy point on Wednesday, and Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL) has been fighting to hold above its most recent buy range, after clearing a buy point at 1006.29. 
China-based video game leader NetEase scrambled up 1.3%. The stock, which gained 60% across 2017, and is extended above a 320.77 buy point in a cup-with-handle base. 
Chip developer Xilinx ( XLNX ) leapt 3.7% after Goldman Sachs upgraded the stock to buy, from neutral. The gain lifted Xilinx back above support at its 10-week moving average, to just below a 73.89 buy point in a double-bottom base. 
Early earnings action was generally not good, with Constellation Brands (STX) down 3%, Greenbrier (GBX) falling 4% and Cal-Maine Foods (CALM) taking a 9% dive after their quarterly results. 
The prime exception was burger joint Sonic (SONC), which served up an early 5% advance. The Oklahoma City-based chain reported mixed fiscal first-quarter earnings after Thursday's close. The gain gave the stock a breakout past a 28.83 buy point in a cup-with-handle base.
